name: Microchip Technology
description: Microchip makes embedded-control chips: mixed-signal microcontrollers (half of sales), analog and interface products, and a third group that includes FPGAs, memory and a technology-licensing business (SuperFlash royalties and IP sales). Customers are electronics makers reached 47 percent through distributors (Arrow alone 12 percent). Sales fell 42 percent in fiscal 2025 (from $7,634.4M to $4,401.6M) as customers and distributors worked off inventory, then recovered to $4,713.1M in fiscal 2026, and the June 2026 quarter was up 38 percent year on year. It carries a $1.485B 7.50 percent mandatory convertible preferred issued March 2025 and pays a common dividend.

businessLines.name: Mixed-signal microcontrollers
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit into embedded-control designs; proprietary parts hold prices relatively stable, and development tools and software lock customers in. Some volume under long-term supply agreements (LTSAs) with customer cash advances.
businessLines.description: 8-, 16- and 32-bit microcontrollers and 32/64-bit embedded microprocessors, plus storage controllers, memory controllers and switches for AI data center and enterprise infrastructure.

businessLines.name: Analog
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit, marketed mainly into the microcontroller and FPGA customer base and to other customers; proprietary parts are price-stable, non-proprietary parts follow supply and demand.
businessLines.description: Power management, linear, mixed-signal, high voltage, thermal management, discrete diodes and MOSFETs, RF, gate drivers, timing, USB, ethernet, interface products.

businessLines.name: Other (FPGA, licensing, memory, services)
businessLines.how: Mix of one-time product sales and recurring licence royalties and fees; IP sales can be lumpy (the 10-K credits some FY2026 growth to sales of certain IP rights).
businessLines.description: FPGAs (low/mid-range, defense-grade), royalties on SuperFlash and other technology licences, sales of intellectual property, engineering services, memory (EEPROM, serial flash, SRAM), timing systems, wafer foundry and assembly/test services, legacy ASICs, aerospace products. Includes the whole technology licensing segment.

brands.share: Licensee revenue $163.8M, 3.5% of FY2026 net sales
